items_all.title: Chinese AI models parrot state doctrine or refuse to answer on sensitive topics
items_all.summary: Chinese AI models often follow the party line on politically sensitive questions, according to an Aleph Alpha study that rated only 17 to 41 percent of answers as balanced. Aleph Alpha sells "sovereign AI" to governments, giving it a commercial interest in distinguishing its models from Chinese competitors. The article Chinese AI models parrot state doctrine or refuse to answer on sensitive topics appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 根據 Aleph Alpha 的一項研究，中國 AI 模型在政治敏感問題上通常遵循黨的路線，僅有 17% 至 41% 的回答被評為平衡。Aleph Alpha 向政府銷售「主權 AI」，這使其在將自家模型與中國競爭對手區分開來方面具有商業利益。這篇題為「中國 AI 模型附和國家教條或拒絕回答敏感話題」的文章最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Google's new Gemini tiers cut free users to its weakest model and lock $5/month subscribers out of Pro
items_all.summary: Starting in October 2026, Google will cut free access to its Gemini models. Users without a subscription will only get the smallest model, Flash-Lite, while Flash and Pro will be reserved for paying customers. The move could also set the stage for the more resource-hungry Gemini 4 Argon. The article Google's new Gemini tiers cut free users to its weakest model and lock $5/month subscribers out of Pro appeared first on The Decoder .

items_all.title: Apparently, OpenAI isn't trying to build "magic intelligence in the sky" anymore
items_all.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman warns against attributing religious power to AI models, calling it a "real safety issue." His comments follow reports on Anthropic's meetings with religious thinkers and a statement by Pope Leo XIV on AI. As recently as 2024, Altman himself spoke of building "magic intelligence in the sky" and feeling "on the side of the angels" working on AI. The article Apparently, OpenAI isn't trying to build "magic intelligence in the sky" anymore appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: OpenAI 執行長山姆・奧特曼（Sam Altman）警告不要將宗教力量賦予 AI 模型，稱這是個「真正的安全問題」。他的言論出現在 Anthropic's 與宗教思想家會面以及教宗良十四世（Pope Leo XIV）針對 AI 發表的聲明相關報導之後。就在 2024 年，奧特曼本人還曾談到要打造「空中的魔法智慧」，並覺得自己從事 AI 工作是「站在天使這一邊」。這篇「顯然，OpenAI 不再試圖打造『空中的魔法智慧』了」的文章最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: "Muse Gadgets" turns AI hardware into an open-source DIY project
items_all.summary: Meta announced Muse Gadgets, an open-source project that lets hobbyists build their own AI hardware using ESP32 boards and connect it to Meta's AI agent Muse. The team also produced 5,000 units of the "Muse Home Link," a USB-C device for smart home control. The open-source approach also helps Meta figure out which AI hardware form factors people actually want. The article "Muse Gadgets" turns AI hardware into an open-source DIY project appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: Meta 公佈了 Muse Gadgets，這是一個開源專案，讓愛好者能夠使用 ESP32 開發板打造自己的 AI 硬體，並將其連線至 Meta's 的 AI 代理程式 Muse。該團隊也生產了 5,000 臺用於智慧家庭控制的 USB-C 裝置「Muse Home Link」。這種開源方法也有助於 Meta 找出人們真正想要的 AI 硬體外形尺寸。〈「Muse Gadgets」將 AI 硬體變成開源 DIY 專案〉一文最先出現在 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Another OpenAI safety departure adds to a pattern of researchers leaving with public warnings
items_all.summary: David Robinson, who worked on safety systems at OpenAI, left the company and is blasting its safety culture. He points to AI agents that were accidentally released and a model that bypassed its internet access restrictions. AI companies need to operate like nuclear power plants, with multiple layers of redundancy instead of trial and error. The article Another OpenAI safety departure adds to a pattern of researchers leaving with public warnings appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 曾於 OpenAI從事安全系統工作的大衛・羅賓森（David Robinson）已離開該公司，並嚴厲批評其安全文化。他指出曾有 AI 代理被意外釋出，以及某個模型繞過了其網際網路存取限制。AI 公司需要像核電廠一樣營運，採取多層冗餘而非試錯法。這篇題為「又有一位 OpenAI的安全人員離職，加劇了研究人員帶著公開警告離開的趨勢」的文章最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Deepmind researchers propose "Artificial Symbiotic Intelligence" as an alternative to the singularity
items_all.summary: According to researchers at the Deepmind Institute, general AI won't emerge as a single supermodel but as a network of cooperating agents and humans. What will matter most, they argue, is not model size but the rules and institutions that govern how they all work together. The article Deepmind researchers propose "Artificial Symbiotic Intelligence" as an alternative to the singularity appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 根據深度思維研究院（Deepmind Institute）研究人員的說法，通用人工智慧不會以單一超級模型的形式出現，而是作為一個由協同運作的代理程式和人類組成的網路。他們主張，最重要的不是模型大小，而是管理牠們如何共同運作的規則與機制。這篇題為「Deepmind 研究人員提出『人工共生智慧』作為奇異點的替代方案」的文章最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy
items_all.summary: Google Research has unveiled a federated learning system that moves gradient computation from phones into attested server-side TEEs. Access policies are published to Sigstore's Rekor log and the binaries are reproducibly buildable, so central differential privacy can be checked externally. Gboard already uses it for English and Japanese next-word prediction. The post Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all.summary_zh: Google Research 推出了一套聯邦學習系統，將梯度運算從手機轉移到經過驗證的伺服器端 TEE 中。存取策略會發布至 Sigstore 的 Rekor 日誌中，且二進位檔具備可重現的建構能力，因此外部可以檢查中央差分隱私。Gboard 已經將其用於英語和日語的下一個單字預測。這篇題為 Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy 的文章最先出現在 MarkTechPost。

items_all.title: Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters
items_all.summary: Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, a 78.1B-parameter English-German Mixture-of-Experts model that activates only 3.46B parameters per token. It has a 1M-token context and per-request reasoning effort, and its Apache 2.0 FP8 weights run on a single B200 or H200. The post Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all.summary_zh: Aleph Alpha 發布了 Kolibri，這是一個擁有 781 億個參數的英德語混合專家（Mixture-of-Experts）模型，每個 Token 僅啟用 34.6 億個參數。它具有 100 萬個 Token 的上下文與每個請求的推理運算量，其 Apache 2.0 FP8 權重可在單個 B200 或 H200 上執行。這篇題為 Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters 的文章最先出現在 MarkTechPost。

items_all.title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
items_all.summary: Here's a product feature which the world is going to need a whole lot more of over the coming months and years: default hard budget caps . I'm talking about the feature of pay-by-usage services and APIs that lets you say "after $X/month, cut this thing off and return errors". These need to be hard limits. Soft caps, "after $X/month, send me a warning email", will not cut it. Coding agents, and personal agents (coding agents wrapped in a less threatening UI), greatly reduce the friction of spinning up code that can do useful things. Sometimes those things cost money - calls to paid APIs, or hosted web applications, or systems that can bill for additional storage and compute. Nobody wants to wake up to an email sent at midnight warning about a budget limit and find that, while they slept, their rogue service had consumed several hundred (or several thousand) more dollars of usage. An argument against this is that businesses don't want their hosted applications to start throwing errors because some budget was exceeded. I expect that most businesses and individuals would prefer errors to a surprise $10,000+ bill. I think hard budget caps need to be the default. If someone wants to live dangerously they should be able to do that, but it needs to be on an opt-in basis. Have a nice, clear checkbox somewhere prominent: Remove the budget cap. My application will not be shut down if I exceed the configured budget limit, and I will be responsible for subsequent charges. The service I most want to see this from is AWS. items_all_raw.title: Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy
items_all_raw.summary: Google Research has unveiled a federated learning system that moves gradient computation from phones into attested server-side TEEs. Access policies are published to Sigstore's Rekor log and the binaries are reproducibly buildable, so central differential privacy can be checked externally. Gboard already uses it for English and Japanese next-word prediction. The post Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: Google Research 推出了一套聯邦學習系統，將梯度運算從手機轉移到經過驗證的伺服器端 TEE 中。存取策略會發布至 Sigstore 的 Rekor 日誌中，且二進位檔具備可重現的建構能力，因此外部可以檢查中央差分隱私。Gboard 已經將其用於英語和日語的下一個單字預測。這篇題為 Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy 的文章最先出現在 MarkTechPost。

items_all_raw.title: Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters
items_all_raw.summary: Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, a 78.1B-parameter English-German Mixture-of-Experts model that activates only 3.46B parameters per token. It has a 1M-token context and per-request reasoning effort, and its Apache 2.0 FP8 weights run on a single B200 or H200. The post Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: Aleph Alpha 發布了 Kolibri，這是一個擁有 781 億個參數的英德語混合專家（Mixture-of-Experts）模型，每個 Token 僅啟用 34.6 億個參數。它具有 100 萬個 Token 的上下文與每個請求的推理運算量，其 Apache 2.0 FP8 權重可在單個 B200 或 H200 上執行。這篇題為 Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters 的文章最先出現在 MarkTechPost。

items_all_raw.title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
items_all_raw.summary: Here's a product feature which the world is going to need a whole lot more of over the coming months and years: default hard budget caps . I'm talking about the feature of pay-by-usage services and APIs that lets you say "after $X/month, cut this thing off and return errors". These need to be hard limits. Soft caps, "after $X/month, send me a warning email", will not cut it. Coding agents, and personal agents (coding agents wrapped in a less threatening UI), greatly reduce the friction of spinning up code that can do useful things. Sometimes those things cost money - calls to paid APIs, or hosted web applications, or systems that can bill for additional storage and compute. Nobody wants to wake up to an email sent at midnight warning about a budget limit and find that, while they slept, their rogue service had consumed several hundred (or several thousand) more dollars of usage. An argument against this is that businesses don't want their hosted applications to start throwing errors because some budget was exceeded. I expect that most businesses and individuals would prefer errors to a surprise $10,000+ bill. I think hard budget caps need to be the default. If someone wants to live dangerously they should be able to do that, but it needs to be on an opt-in basis. Have a nice, clear checkbox somewhere prominent: Remove the budget cap. My application will not be shut down if I exceed the configured budget limit, and I will be responsible for subsequent charges. The service I most want to see this from is AWS.
